items.title: How to Institutionalize and Individualize Educational Programs to Prevent Violence
items.abstract: We need to build broader, comprehensive and well-established curricula incorporating violence prevention along with other life skills, prevention practices, health information, character building and decision-making. We might be able to take advantage of the curricular revolution that is likely to arrive soon. This revolution will be from the greater deployment of artificial intelligence to personalize the learning process. Strategies are needed to overcome the obstacles to the collaborations required to create these comprehensive curricula. Evaluations are needed of these comprehensive approaches.

items.title: Human Freedom as Participation in Divine Creativity: The Spiritual Intelligence AI Cannot Possess
items.abstract: Contemporary debates on artificial intelligence increasingly raise questions not only about machine agency but also about the nature of human creativity and freedom. While much of the current discussion evaluates AI by comparing its observable behaviour with that of human beings, this article argues that the decisive question is metaphysical rather than functional. Drawing on insights into the nature of freedom from Augustine, Aquinas, and other medieval theologians, I argue that human freedom arises from the rational creature’s participation in an immaterial mode of being that grounds the free agentic self-movement. This participatory account of freedom provides a theological anthropology capable of distinguishing human creativity from increasingly sophisticated artificial systems without appealing merely to current technological limitations. After examining two recent attempts to attribute free agency to AI systems, including theories rooted in intentionality and computational sourcehood, I argue that these accounts fail to identify the metaphysical conditions required for genuinely free and creative agency. Human freedom is shown to be inseparable from the unity of the spiritual soul, whose intellect and will participate in divine wisdom and providence with a specific kind of secondary causality. Thus, I identify the distinctive feature of human agentic intelligence in its intrinsic transcendent teleology, a mark of participation in the divine. AI systems, even their most autonomous future versions, seem limited by an intrinsic immanent teleology to their algorithmic boundaries. Thus, if my distinction holds, I determine that AI systems may increasingly reproduce the external operations associated with human intelligence and free agency, but they cannot participate in the kind of creative self-movement that belongs to rational creatures created in the image of God. The article concludes that the chief challenge posed by AI is therefore not whether machines will become human, but whether technological culture will encourage humanity to reinterpret itself according to computational categories rather than its vocation to participate in divine creativity.

items.title: Human-AI collaboration in crisis response: understanding adoption barriers and enablers for generative AI in emergency decision-making
items.abstract: Abstract Human-AI collaboration in emergency management represents a critical socio-technical challenge that requires understanding both technological capabilities and human factors. This study examines the barriers and enablers influencing emergency decision-makers’ adoption of generative artificial intelligence, focusing on the complex interplay between individual, organizational, and technological factors in high-stakes crisis environments. Through expert interviews and intuitionistic fuzzy DEMATEL analysis involving Chinese emergency management practitioners, we identify five key dimensions affecting AI adoption: technology acceptance, decision-making processes, contextual factors, risk and trust, and individual factors. Our analysis within the Chinese emergency management context suggests that contextual factors and decision-making processes are perceived as primary drivers, while technology acceptance and individual factors serve as critical enablers shaped by organizational environments. The findings demonstrate that successful human-AI collaboration requires addressing social and technical dimensions simultaneously, with organizational support, trust-building, and individual self-efficacy emerging as fundamental requirements. These insights inform strategies for emergency management organizations to enhance human-AI integration through governance frameworks, transparency mechanisms, and targeted training programs, contributing empirical evidence to the growing literature on socio-technical aspects of AI adoption in critical decision-making contexts.

items.title: Human-AI Collaboration in SMEs: A Role-Sensitive Framework for Cognitive Enterprise Hubs
items.abstract: Traditional enterprise automation systems often lack the contextual intelligence and flexibility required in logistics-intensive environments, particularly for small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SME). This paper proposes a fivephase implementation framework for Cognitive En- terprise Hubs (CEH), emphasizing role-sensitive deployment and continuous alignment between human and Artificial Intelligence (AI). The model combines architectural planning, AI integration and cultural adaptation to support scalable and adaptive collaboration across federated ecosystems. Empirical validation is provided through two crosssector case studies and a multi-role survey with 18 participants from IT, cybersecurity and telecommunications sectors. Findings reveal notable perceptual differences across organizational roles, especially between IT leaders, transformation strategists and frontline employees, regarding CEH impact on productivity, support and future opportunities. The study underscores that CEH success depends not only on technical orchestration but also on socio-cultural alignment. To address this, we offer practical deployment guidelines tailored for SME and logistics-driven operations. By integrating technical and organizational perspectives, this work advances the practical deployment of intelligent enterprise systems, positioning CEH as enablers of inclusive, cognitively enhanced coordination frameworks.

items.title: Human-Centered AI Across the Atlantic
items.abstract: This chapter examines human-centered artificial intelligence (AI) governance in higher education through a comparative analysis of the United States and the United Kingdom. Drawing on a light institutional logics perspective, this chapter explores how differing policy environments, institutional priorities, and accountability structures shape university responses to emerging AI technologies. Rather than positioning AI implementation as a primarily technical challenge, the chapter argues that meaningful integration depends on how institutions distribute responsibility, preserve educator agency, and develop shared expectations among stakeholders. Particular attention is given to tensions surrounding technological adoption, academic integrity, assessment practices, AI literacy, and educator capacity. This chapter highlights the need to move beyond techno-solutionist approaches by developing governance structures that support critical engagement, transparent decision-making, and sustainable human-centered practices.

items.title: Human-in-the-Loop AI for resilient supply chain operations: a framework for augmented decision-making and ethical deployment
items.abstract: Purpose This research examines how Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) artificial intelligence (AI) can support resilient decision-making, operational performance, transparency, trust and ethical accountability in operations and supply chain management (OSCM). Design/methodology/approach The research adopts a design science research approach combined with comparative case analysis. A HITL AI framework, termed the adaptive oversight architecture (AOA), was developed and evaluated in two contrasting OSCM contexts. System logs, operational observations, interviews and performance indicators were analysed to examine decision outcomes, human oversight, trust and accountability. Findings HITL integration was associated with improved exception-handling accuracy, reduced human override frequency, shorter task-completion times and higher user satisfaction across the two cases. Qualitative findings further indicate that trust calibration, training, interface design, workflow integration and organizational governance influence how effectively human oversight operates. The findings also identify risks of automation dependence, accountability diffusion and inappropriate reliance on algorithmic recommendations. Research limitations/implications The research is limited to two case firms, which constrains the generalizability of the findings. While the dual-case approach provides in-depth insights, broader studies involving larger datasets or cross-industry comparisons are needed to validate the proposed framework. Future research could extend the empirical base by employing longitudinal analysis, simulations or hybrid models that test HITL effectiveness under different operational conditions. These directions will allow for a more comprehensive understanding of the scalability, adaptability and long-term organizational impacts of HITL-enabled supply chains. Practical implications For practitioners, the research highlights how HITL can be implemented to strengthen supply chain decision-making while ensuring compliance with ethical and regulatory standards. It suggests that organizations should prioritize training programs, design user-friendly interfaces and establish override mechanisms to maximize HITL effectiveness. The findings emphasize the importance of aligning AI investments with human oversight structures, rather than pursuing automation in isolation. Managers can use the framework to evaluate readiness, map decision tasks suitable for HITL integration and design workflows that balance speed, transparency and accountability. Social implications By positioning humans as active collaborators, HITL contributes to responsible AI adoption that safeguards jobs, reinforces accountability and reduces risks of algorithmic bias in supply chain operations. The approach ensures that technology complements rather than replaces human expertise, fostering inclusive digital transformation. From a societal perspective, embedding ethical safeguards into AI decision-making promotes trust in enterprise systems and enhances their legitimacy. The findings encourage the development of AI solutions that not only drive operational efficiency but also align with broader social values of fairness, responsibility and human dignity. Originality/value This research conceptualizes HITL as a dynamic socio-technical arrangement rather than a static control mechanism. The proposed AOA explains how human authority, algorithmic decision-making and organizational governance interact through oversight, trust calibration and distributed accountability, providing a mechanism-based conceptualization of HITL for OSCM.

items.title: Human–AI Collaboration in Higher Education: Faculty Readiness and Institutional Transformation—A Semantic Review and Bibliometric Mapping
items.abstract: Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, is changing how academic work is planned, produced, assessed, communicated, and governed. Yet adoption is uneven: individual faculty members may experiment with AI while institutional workload models, assessment systems, professional development, and governance remain largely unchanged. This paper examines how human–AI collaboration, faculty readiness, and institutional change interact in higher education. Drawing on a semantic synthesis of literature already cited in the supplied data, the paper organises relevant work around five connected themes: AI literacy and faculty capability; task-level human–AI collaboration; professional identity and trust; organisational culture and change capability; and responsible governance. It proposes a transparent protocol for future bibliometric mapping. Importantly, this is a conceptual semantic review, not a completed database-based bibliometric study: no publication counts, co-citation networks, or keyword frequencies are reported as empirical findings. The synthesis suggests that faculty readiness is multidimensional and cannot be reduced to tool familiarity. It includes pedagogical judgement, critical evaluation of AI outputs, ethical awareness, disciplinary adaptation, and confidence to disclose and contest AI-supported decisions. Institutional change requires leadership, protected development time, policy clarity, peer learning, workload recognition, assessment redesign, and participatory governance. A conceptual framework links institutional conditions to faculty readiness, the quality of human–AI collaboration, and feedback into organisational strategy. The paper offers a practical readiness matrix and implementation pathway for higher education institutions, including Indian institutions navigating digital transformation. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence; Higher Education; Academic Work; Faculty Readiness; Human–AI Collaboration; Institutional Change; AI Literacy; Semantic Review

items.abstract: Hybrid Intelligence for Industrial Process Optimization: Establishing the Need Presentation delivered at the 23rd International Conference on Informatics in Control, Automation and Robotics (ICINCO 2026) within the Special Session on Hybrid Artificial Intelligence (HybAI 2026) held in Angers, France, October 26–28, 2026. Summary:Over 80% of industrial artificial intelligence proofs-of-concept (PoCs) stall or fail to reach production due to a fundamental structural mismatch: physical plants operate under rigorous thermodynamic and hydraulic conservation laws with zero fault tolerance, whereas pure data-driven machine learning models act as unconstrained black boxes omitting causal mechanisms. This presentation opens the HybAI 2026 Special Session by surveying the theoretical and practical imperatives for Hybrid Intelligence: Limits of Pure Data-Driven AI: Why the No Free Lunch theorem and severe physical exploration budgets make learning physics ab initio sample-inefficient and hazardous in production. Critique of Sutton's "Bitter Lesson": In digital games, simulation and trial-and-error exploration are computationally free; in municipal water systems and heavy industry, unconstrained exploration destroys hardware (pipe bursts, pump cavitation). Physical invariants are indispensable inductive scaffolds, not bottlenecks. Lessons from Neurorobotics: How biological motor control decomposes known morphological kinematics from state-dependent disturbance estimation, providing a direct design template for industrial gray-box digital twins. Acausal Physics & Differentiable SciML: Unifying Differential-Algebraic Equations (DAEs) with adjoint sensitivity analysis to guarantee safety and sample efficiency by design. items.title: iHELP: Intelligent Holistic Emergency Logistics Platform. A Cloud-Based Simulation-Optimization Platform for Disaster Logistics and Real-Time Situational Awareness
items.abstract: Natural disasters increasingly cause severe casualties, displacement, and economic destruction, yet emergency response operations are routinely hindered by fragmented inter-agency coordination, resource planning bottlenecks, and information limited to overwhelmed traditional communication channels. To address these operational challenges, this chapter presents the Intelligent Holistic Emergency Logistics Platform (iHELP), a cloud-based simulation-optimization system designed to coordinate multi-modal supply chains and provide real-time situational awareness during emergencies. Abstracting the challenge as a multi-commodity, multi-mode transportation problem, iHELP models the assignment, routing, and scheduling of heterogeneous vehicle fleets across ground, air, and maritime networks under dynamic operational constraints. To overcome data scarcity during emergencies, iHELP incorporates a dedicated Social Media Analytics Module that uses natural language processing, computer vision, and spatial clustering to ingest user posts, filter misinformation, compute confidence metrics, and infer urgent humanitarian needs. Additional integrated modules manage weather disruptions, service prioritization, and infrastructure availability. Decision-makers interact with the system via a web dashboard that visualizes animated operations, transporter utilization, and inventory trends. Developed and validated in collaboration with NATO’s Crisis Management and Disaster Response Center of Excellence through simulated flood response scenarios, iHELP demonstrates strong capability in delivering robust, high-quality emergency logistics plans under stress and uncertainty.

items.title: Implementing AI-Assisted Diabetic Retinopathy Screening: A Qualitative Evidence Synthesis of Data Governance, Trust and Equity
items.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy can be screened (assisted by artificial intelligence) in primary care and underserved contexts, and technical accuracy is irrelevant to whether patients and practitioners consider the service a legitimate offer.This secondary qualitative research study explored how trust, data ownership and equity are formed in empirical descriptions of AI-assisted retinal screening.A systematic search found 35 sources from 2016-2026.The findings were based on sixteen major articles published since 2021, whereas a different body informed the introduction, theoretical framework, research gap, methods and discussion of literature.This yielded three themes suggested by reflexive thematic synthesis: trust as a relational goal and not an assurance of accuracy alone; retinal data ownership is an open relationship of governance; equity is a dilemma of increased access and risk redistribution.Speed, convenience, and instant outcomes were well-regarded by patients, although this consideration faded as AI seemed to substitute clinical elucidation or reuse of data was opaque.Practitioners were open to AI when accountability, escalation channels, and training could be perceived, but raised anxieties over consent, accountability, information security, and skewed model performance.The greatest gains in access were most effective when AI was integrated within attainable care pathways, though inaccessible images, referral failure, digital savvy, and subgroup bias could recreate disparity.The paper finds that reliable AI eye screening entails human-controllable communication, purpose-driven data stewardship, and equity considerations throughout the screening process, not just at the algorithmic endpoint.The analytic focus is therefore multi-actor and system-level, integrating patient experience with practitioner readiness, institutional accountability, data governance and referral capacity.

items.abstract: This study proposes an organizational and economic framework for improving ERP-based integrated management in industrial enterprises, with particular emphasis on Uzbekistan's machinery manufacturing sector. It examines opportunities to enhance the integration of information systems, strengthen coordination among procurement, warehousing, and production operations, and improve the adaptability of conventional static inventory management policies. The proposed framework combines the integration of existing Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) functions, multi-model bills of materials (BOMs), feedback from Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), dynamic calculations of safety stock and reorder points, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted decision support under human supervision. An economic optimization model incorporates inventory holding costs, procurement costs, material shortage costs, and costs associated with production interruptions. Static and dynamic inventory management policies are compared using operational and economic performance indicators. The study presents a conceptual framework and an analytical evaluation methodology; empirical validation at the enterprise level requires actual production, inventory, and procurement data.

items.title: Improving Patient-Reported Understanding of Radiographic Reports in Spine Surgery Through Implementation of Natural Language Processing: A Randomized Controlled Study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Many spinal imaging reports are written above recommended health literacy levels, limiting patient comprehension at a time when rapid electronic access to radiology results is increasing. We aim to evaluate whether supplemental natural language processing (NLP)–modified radiology reports—within the context of usual patient portal access to the original report—are associated with improved patient-reported perceived understandability compared with standard reports among patients undergoing spine imaging. METHODS: This is a prospective randomized controlled study with limited participant blinding, conducted with 2 spine surgeons affiliated with a single academic medical center in New York City. Participants (18 years or older) undergoing spine imaging at initial surgical consultation were enrolled and were randomized to receive either their original radiology report or a supplemental NLP–modified version. Radiology reports were rewritten using a standardized natural language processing prompt (ChatGPT 4.0) and reviewed for accuracy by study investigators. The primary outcome was survey-based patient-reported perceived understandability. Secondary outcomes included objective readability scores (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Flesch Reading Ease, Simple Measure of Gobbledygook, Gunning-Fog Index). RESULTS: Fifty-two adults were enrolled; 42 (81%) completed the postintervention survey. Among 52 randomized participants (26 women [50%]), NLP–modified reports demonstrated significantly improved objective readability across all indices compared with original reports (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, 5.9 ± 1.1 vs 11.0 ± 1.7; Reading Ease, 71.0 ± 10.3 vs 28.2 ± 12.5; Simple Measure of Gobbledygook, 20.1 ± 12.7 vs 23.5 ± 15.7; Gunning-Fog Index, 8.2 ± 1.1 vs 14.3 ± 1.8; all P < .01). Of 42 survey respondents, those receiving supplemental NLP-modified reports reported greater ease of understanding the report language (4.2 ± 1.2 vs 2.6 ± 1.5, mean-difference 95% CI: 0.75-2.53, P < .01, Bonferroni-corrected- P = .02), and less difficulty with medical terms (2.0 ± 1.5 vs 3.6 ± 1.4, mean-difference 95% CI: −2.51 to −0.60, P < .01, Bonferroni-corrected- P = .04). CONCLUSION: Supplemental NLP-modified radiology reports were associated with improved objective readability and higher patient-reported perceived ease of understanding in a spine surgery initial consultation setting. These findings support further investigation of NLP-generated supplemental explanations within supervised clinical workflows.

AI is a rapidly developing field and can transform many industries and aspects of daily life. Applications of AI in the industrial field are accompanied by automation of production, energy saving, increased safety, and the creation of new technological capabilities. items.title: Influence of Formative Assessment Guidelines on Students’ Academic Achievement: Evidence from Public Secondary Schools in Kigoma Municipality, Tanzania
items.abstract: Formative assessment is widely regarded as a cornerstone of students’ academic achievement, but its implementation at the classroom level is jeopardised by inconsistent guidelines. This study examined the influence of formative assessment guidelines on students’ academic achievement in public secondary schools in Kigoma Municipality, Tanzania. The study employed a convergent research design under a mixed-methods approach to collect data from 169 respondents. A total of 156 students were selected using simple random sampling, six teachers experienced in using formative assessments, six academic masters/mistresses, and one education officer. Data were collected using questionnaires for students and interviews for educators. The quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics (frequencies, percentages, and means) using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) version 20 with a tested reliability coefficient of 0.713, while qualitative data were analysed using a deductive content analysis approach. The findings indicate that students valued weekly tests and clear teacher instructions as motivating and fair mechanisms that enhanced students’ academic achievement. Teachers also reported that classroom assessment guidelines are useful, but the guidelines lack competence-based clarity. Further, students prioritise formative assessments over national examinations, while socioeconomic limitations undermine the effectiveness of take-home assignments. The study concludes that the use of formative assessment guidelines improves academic achievement, but challenges in teacher preparation and policy-practice alignment persist. The use of technology in formative assessment is limited by infrastructure and connectivity; additionally, the study concludes that increased use of artificial intelligence and the internet is not a feasible option for public secondary schools in Kigoma Municipality. Therefore, policymakers should emphasise capacity-building initiatives for teachers and administrators in competence-based curriculum assessment methods. The shift from traditional teaching and learning approaches to competence-based models is often hindered by resource constraints or shortages. Emphasis on critical thinking should begin at the classroom level and support students’ academic achievement rather than merely high grades in final assessments.

items.title: INNOVATIVE DIGITAL BANKING TECHNOLOGIES AND THEIR IMPACT ON THE TRANSFORMATION OF BANKING ACTIVITIES
items.abstract: The article examines innovative digital banking technologies as a key factor in the transformation of modern banking activities and the modification of traditional banking business models. The contemporary technological foundations of digital banking are considered, including artificial intelligence and machine learning, Big Data and data analytics, cloud technologies, APIs and Open Banking, robotic process automation, digital identification, modern payment technologies, and blockchain. Current trends in the digitalization of the Ukrainian banking sector are analyzed, including the development of cashless payments, the increasing adoption of contactless and tokenized payment instruments, the expansion of digital payment infrastructure, the formation of a regulatory framework for Open Banking, and the growing use of artificial intelligence technologies. It is substantiated that the digital transformation of banking activities is comprehensive in nature and involves a gradual transition from technological modernization to business process automation, personalized customer service, and the transformation of banks’ business models. The main transformational effects of innovative technologies are systematized, including increased operational efficiency, reduced service delivery time, expanded accessibility of financial products, improved customer experience, enhanced quality of managerial decision-making, and improved risk management systems. The key challenges of digital transformation are identified, including cyber risks, data protection, technological dependence, model risks associated with the use of artificial intelligence. The necessity of assessing the effectiveness of digitalization not only in terms of the scale of technology adoption but also according to its economic, customerrelated, operational, and risk-related effects is substantiated. The promising areas for the development of digital banking in Ukraine are identified, including the wider application of artificial intelligence, the development of Open Banking and Open Finance, the formation of digital ecosystems, the expansion of embedded finance, cloud technologies, and intelligent automation.

items.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics into Marketing Education: The Digital-Ready Marketing Education Framework for Developing Graduates in Emerging Economies
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and data analytics are reshaping marketing practice, yet many universities in emerging economies have been slow to reflect these changes in their curricula. Limited digital infrastructure, inadequate faculty expertise, and concerns about the ethical use of AI continue to constrain curriculum reform. This study develops the DigitalReady Marketing Education Framework (DRMEF) to guide the integration of AI and data analytics into marketing education. Drawing on a conceptual theory-building approach, the study synthesizes literature on AI, marketing education, technology adoption, and digital competency development. The analysis shows that effective integration depends on four closely connected elements: digital infrastructure, curriculum redesign, faculty capability, and ethical AI governance. The framework highlights that preparing graduates for data-driven marketing requires more than technology adoption; it also demands institutional commitment and continuous curriculum development, offering a practical guide for higher education institutions in emerging economies.

items.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Quantum Physics into Islamic Education: Opportunities, Challenges, and a Framework for Future Learning
items.abstract: Islamic educational institutions are increasingly drawn into a technological moment shaped by artificial intelligence and, more quietly, by quantum physics, yet little research asks how either can be woven into Islamic pedagogy without unsettling tawhid, the epistemological commitment underlying the tradition. This PRISMA-guided systematic review maps the opportunities, challenges, and design principles for integrating AI and quantum physics into Islamic education and proposes a working framework. Of 1,563 unique records retrieved from five databases (2016-2025), 57 studies were retained: 48 engaging directly with an Islamic-education context (Stream A), and 9 general quantum-physics-education studies included deliberately as a comparison corpus (Stream B), since none met a joint Islamic-context-and-quantum criterion. AI is used mainly for personalised Qur'anic and Arabic-language learning and administrative efficiency; quantum content remains almost entirely confined to secular STEM curricula. Data privacy, algorithmic bias, teacher readiness, and decontextualised content recur as concerns. The review proposes the AI-Quantum-Islamic Education Framework (AIQIEF), grounding adoption in tawhid-based epistemology rather than treating these technologies as neutral add-ons.

items.title: Integrating predictive modeling, imaging, and EHR-linked decision support in spine informatics
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming spine care by enabling analysis of imaging, clinical, and textual data to support diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment planning. Techniques including deep learning–based image analysis, radiomics, and natural language processing (NLP) offer opportunities to standardize interpretation and derive quantitative biomarkers beyond human visual assessment. This narrative review examines recent innovations in spine-focused biomedical informatics and evaluates their clinical relevance and translational challenges. A narrative review was conducted, focusing on AI in spine care across imaging, radiomics, NLP of electronic health records, and clinical decision support. Literature was selected via targeted PubMed searches; studies describing technical development, validation, and clinical implementation were synthesized, addressing explainability, uncertainty, workflow, and regulation. Convolutional neural networks enable vertebral and disc segmentation, detection of degenerative and traumatic pathology, and quantitative assessment of paraspinal musculature. Radiomics approaches extract high-dimensional imaging features that improve the prediction of osteoporosis, fracture risk, tumor characterization, and surgical outcomes. NLP techniques, including emerging large language models, unlock clinically relevant information from unstructured text, enhancing outcome prediction and population-level analyses. Multimodal clinical decision support systems integrating imaging, EHR data, and NLP-derived features demonstrate promise for personalized risk assessment and treatment guidance. Challenges remain regarding data heterogeneity, generalizability, privacy, and prospective validation. AI-driven biomedical informatics holds substantial promise to enhance diagnostic accuracy, prognostication, and personalized decision-making in spine care. Successful clinical translation will require robust validation, explainable, uncertainty-aware models, regulatory alignment, and integration into clinical workflows to ensure safe, trustworthy, and patient-centered adoption.

items.title: Integration of Artificial Intelligence and Mental Health Education
items.abstract: Mental health education for university students faces challenges, like inadequate personalization and delayed intervention. This study develops an intelligent platform integrating artificial intelligence and big data. The platform comprises structured courses, an artificial intelligence psychological assistant, self-assessment tools, and personalized recommendation functions, with core logic centered on resource classification, optimization, and dynamic mining. A quasi-experiment was conducted with 386 undergraduates for eight weeks, followed by a three-month follow-up. Results show the experimental group significantly outperformed the control group in mental health literacy, help-seeking attitudes, and emotional regulation self-efficacy (p < 0.001), with effects persisting long-term. Platform usage intensity positively moderated intervention effects, and high-engagement users gained the most. This study verifies the platform's effectiveness in optimizing mental health information resource management, providing a feasible digital solution for university mental health education.

items.title: Integration of artificial intelligence in quality improvement projects for undergraduate nursing students: Enhancing nursing education through innovative applications
items.abstract: Background and objective: Nursing faculty have been hesitant to incorporate artificial intelligence into coursework due to various reasons, including the risk of affecting academic integrity and the potential for receiving inaccurate information. As nursing cohorts continue to grow, innovative approaches are needed to meet learning objectives; such as artificial intelligence. Incorporating artificial intelligence into group projects may increase responsible, ethical, and critical use of artificial intelligence and support programs in managing larger cohorts. The purpose of this initiative was to integrate artificial intelligence into the literature review process for a quality improvement group project to develop students’ ability to use artificial intelligence responsibly, ethically, and critically. This approach included validating the accuracy of artificial intelligence generated information. Methods: This initiative was offered as an honors conversion opportunity within the Clinical Science II course to undergraduate nursing students. Six students opted to participate and were divided into two groups of three. Groups selected a topic related to the course content and aligned it with one of the Joint Commission national patient safety goals. Groups developed a clinical question, search strategy, conducted a literature review, and used artificial intelligence to identify evidence. Results: Benefits of using artificial intelligence included the generation of creative ideas, provision of workflow steps, and a broad range of solutions. Challenges included a lack of concrete examples and a tendency for artificial intelligence generated information to be more practical than theoretical. Groups found artificial intelligence generated findings aligned with most articles from their literature reviews. Conclusions: Incorporating the utilization of artificial intelligence into nursing curriculums can help programs monitor usage while managing growing cohorts. Allowing students to engage with artificial intelligence under guided instruction enhances understanding of its practical applications in clinical settings. This will better prepare students for real-world practice while ensuring academic integrity is maintained.

items.title: Integration of HVAC Systems with Interior Design for Sustainable and Comfortable Living Spaces
items.abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable buildings and healthier indoor environments has transformed the role of Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems from conventional mechanical services into integral components of architectural and interior design strategies. Modern occupants spend a significant portion of their lives indoors, making indoor environmental quality (IEQ), thermal comfort, air quality, and energy efficiency essential considerations in contemporary living spaces. Traditionally, HVAC systems and interior design were developed as separate disciplines, often resulting in conflicts between aesthetic objectives, spatial functionality, and mechanical performance. However, recent approaches emphasize interdisciplinary collaboration between architects, interior designers, and HVAC engineers to create environments that are both environmentally responsible and occupant-centric. This review paper explores the integration of HVAC systems with interior design for achieving sustainable and comfortable living spaces. The study examines the influence of spatial planning, building materials, furniture arrangement, ventilation strategies, smart control technologies, and energy-efficient HVAC solutions on indoor comfort and sustainability. The paper discusses how emerging technologies such as Internet of Things (IoT)-based sensors, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven control systems, and building automation platforms enable adaptive environmental management. Furthermore, the research highlights the importance of considering HVAC requirements during the early stages of interior design development to optimize energy performance, improve indoor air quality, and enhance user experience. The integration of HVAC systems with interior design represents a multidisciplinary approach where technology, environmental responsibility, and human-centered design converge. Future sustainable interiors will depend on intelligent HVAC solutions that respond dynamically to occupant needs while minimizing energy consumption and environmental impact.

items.title: Integration of Smart Home Technologies in Modern Interior Design: A Review of Automated Building Services
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies has transformed residential environments from conventional static spaces into intelligent, adaptive, and interconnected ecosystems. Smart home technologies integrating the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), sensor networks, cloud computing, and automated building services are increasingly influencing contemporary interior design practices. Unlike traditional interior design approaches that primarily focus on spatial aesthetics, functionality, and occupant comfort, smart interiors introduce dynamic interaction between users, architectural components, and automated environmental systems. This review critically examines the integration of smart home technologies into modern interior design with particular emphasis on automated building services, including intelligent lighting, smart heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC), security systems, energy management, automated shading, and adaptive furniture systems. A systematic literature review approach was adopted to analyse recent research from Scopus-indexed journals, ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, and Taylor & Francis databases. The review identifies that smart home development has progressed from simple automation systems toward AI-driven adaptive environments capable of predicting occupant behaviour, optimizing energy consumption, and enhancing residential comfort. Smart lighting and HVAC systems demonstrate significant potential for reducing energy demand, while IoT-based monitoring platforms enable real-time management of indoor environmental quality. Furthermore, emerging technologies such as digital twins, edge computing, smart materials, and robotics are expected to redefine future interior design practices. However, several challenges remain, including interoperability limitations, cybersecurity risks, privacy concerns, high implementation costs, and insufficient integration between technology developers and design professionals. The paper argues that future smart interiors should adopt a human-centred approach where automation remains supportive rather than dominant. This review provides an interdisciplinary framework connecting interior design, building automation, artificial intelligence, and sustainable development, contributing to the emerging field of intelligent residential environments.

items.title: Inteligencia artificial y sostenibilidad educativa en la educación superior virtual
items.abstract: Virtual higher education seeks to address the growing demand for sustainable, inclusive, and ethical educational models within the context of digital transformation and the progressive integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI). The purpose of this study is to analyze the pedagogical, ethical, and organizational conditions required for the implementation of AI applications related to academic tutoring and student monitoring from the perspective of educational sustainability. The research adopts a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design. The quantitative phase consists of a questionnaire using Likert-scale items administered to students, faculty members, and academic tutors, followed by a qualitative phase based on semi-structured interviews aimed at exploring in greater depth the perceptions, experiences, and tensions identified during the quantitative stage. The discussion is structured around four key dimensions: institutional ethical governance, AI-supported academic tutoring, digital inclusion, and systematic evaluation. The findings suggest that AI can contribute to ensuring the continuity of students’ educational pathways, enhancing personalized learning experiences, and enabling the early identification of academic risks. However, it may also give rise to challenges related to privacy, algorithmic bias, surveillance, technological dependency, and the displacement of professional judgment. The study concludes that AI can effectively contribute to educational sustainability only if it is implemented as a transparent decision-support tool that complements, rather than replaces, human judgment while ensuring data protection, accessibility, faculty oversight, and institutional accountability.

items.title: Introduction
items.abstract: Drug discovery and safety testing are complicated time-consuming processes marked by expensive nature and failure at late stage. Conventional experimental and animal methods tend to have low predictive validity and low human outcome translation. The latest advances in artificial intelligence, such as machine learning, deep learning, and data-driven modelling are changing the pharmaceutical value chain, as they allow to identify the target more efficiently, design the molecule, predictive pharmacology, and proactive safety assessment of the drug. This introductory chapter gives an overview of the development of drug discovery and toxicology towards AI-enabled paradigms. It analyses the principles of AI, the contribution of multimodal data integration, and the application in discovery, pharmacology, toxicology, and pharmacovigilance. The regulatory expectations, ethical considerations, and the existing issues pertaining to data quality, model interpretability, and clinical translation are also addressed in the chapter.

items.title: Investigating human and organizational risk propagation in ship foundering: A data-driven HFACS–Apriori–DEMATEL–FCM framework
items.abstract: Maritime foundering is a low-frequency but high-consequence accident mode associated with multiple human, technical, supervisory, and organizational vulnerabilities. This study develops a data-driven framework integrating an adapted Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS), Apriori association rule mining, the Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL), and a Fuzzy Cognitive Map (FCM). A database of 155 foundering investigation reports from the China Maritime Safety Administration was coded into 50 risk factors. Apriori association mining identified empirical conditional associations in the coded reports, and their confidence values were used to parameterize the subsequent DEMATEL and FCM analyses. The modeled results distinguish highly activated terminal vulnerability accumulators from upstream intervention factors. Under the baseline FCM settings, idealized suppression of substandard physical and mental condition (P10), a lagging emergency response mechanism (O11), and the absence of an emergency preparedness plan (S8) yielded the largest reductions in aggregate activation across the remaining factors, with Global Sensitivity Index magnitudes of approximately 0.124–0.136. The findings support cross-level safety interventions that target latent organizational, supervisory, and preconditional vulnerabilities before they propagate into foundering.

items.title: Invisible patterns of motivation: AI-assisted qualitative analysis of cover letters of teacher-education applicants
items.abstract: Abstract The aim of this study is to explore motivational patterns in teacher candidates' cover letters (CL) and to examine the methodological role of artificial intelligence (AI) in qualitative content analysis. The theoretical framework is provided by the literature on teacher career motivation, qualitative text analysis, and the latest approaches to AI-based content analysis. The empirical analysis is based on the CLs of teacher training applicants. The analysis uses deductive coding, employing both human coders and an AI-based analytical system. The aim of the text analysis is to identify the dominant motivational factors and construct a motivational factor structure. The qualitative results are supplemented at an early stage by quantitative analysis, which examines the relationships between the identified motivational factors and the selected background variables. The methodological contribution of the study lies in the use of AI-assisted pre-coding within a deductive qualitative framework combined with systematic human validation. The results show that the most dominant motivational factors for teacher candidates are 1. Love of teaching, 2. Internal interest, 3. Shaping the next generation, 4. Career adjustment. Automated screening indicated that, on average, approximately 20% of the analysed text was flagged as potentially AI-generated. Potential AI-assisted writing may affect the linguistic and stylistic characteristics of the letters.

items.abstract: The increasing involvement of the emotional Artificial Intelligence and affective computing in child-oriented digital space has revolutionized the organization of persuasion, engagement and consumption. This chapter reviews mood-responsive marketing systems, which deduce and respond to the emotional state of children in real-time, a concept known as invisible persuasion to explain the influence of algorithmic marketing at the unconscious level. Basing the analysis on the interdisciplinary theory and recent case studies of educational platforms and smart toy ecosystems, the analysis indicates how the emotional inference, adaptive reward calibration, and loops of reinforcement influence engagement and dependency. The chapter points out the ethical, psychological and governance issues stating that AI design should be emotionally responsible, protecting the autonomy of children, their well-being, and limits of their development.

items.title: Is conscious experience a complex adaptive system of narratives, that is, a cultural artifact?
items.abstract: We know that biology’s almost astronomical complexity can, in principle, be explained by the paradigm of natural selection, together with John Holland’s new paradigm of an emergent hierarchy of increasingly complex adaptive systems (CASs). This paper shows that these two paradigms might also explain conscious experience, an explanation that, though anticipated by the narratologist Bernini, has not heretofore been clarified. Paradigm shifts happen slowly. Current research on CASs mainly uses computer simulations and mathematics to explore the properties of existing CASs. This paper draws upon the well-understood hierarchy of biological CASs to propose its extension into a psychological hierarchy that includes narrative and hence, conscious experience. Psychoanalyst Daniel Stern’s observational studies show that, in human breast feeding, a narrative emerges from biology. As an infant, you internalized your care-giver’s experience of you to initiate your experience of yourself. Observational studies of adults in therapy groups further argue that conscious experience is a CAS that emerges from interacting narratives. Clark and Chalmers showed that the brain has developed cultural artifacts to extend its capacity, examples being music, language, and narrative. Therefore consciousness would also be a cultural artifact. Current neuroscientific theories of consciousness (ToCs), limited by Crick’s materialist ‘astonishing hypothesis,’ seek to explain consciousness in terms of neural processing. This paper’s relational hypothesis is more plausible. This paper’s ToC overlaps with three out of Seth and Bayne’s (2023) four main classes of neuroscientific ToCs. It meets Seth and Bayne’s criteria for support by making two confirmed predictions, one about autism, the other about dreams (autism and dreams both disturb experience), that the four classes of neuroscientific ToCs fail to make. This paper’s ToC has implications for the development of artificial intelligence.

items.title: La inteligencia artificial en universidades, reflexión para la filosofía de la ciencia y la sostenibilidad
items.abstract: University classrooms are where students acquire higher-level knowledge and develop skills for future professional development in a work environment that requires decision-making through analysis, synthesis, and evaluation. Artificial intelligence provides guidance to students as a support tool, but there is a risk that it may become invasive or substitute for solving, thinking, and dictating what should or can be done, resulting in negative impacts and generating significant risks. The objective is to investigate students' reflections of artificial intelligence for their proper training, which must consciously consider sustainability and the importance of the philosophy of science to position it as a technological advancement. The paradigm is qualitative, as it involves discussion and the speculative aspects of the philosophy of science. Worksheets and a Likert scale were used to collect information. The results show that approximately 35% of respondents agree on the positive and negative aspects of its use, highlighting risks and benefits. The most radical position, which defends artificial intelligence, is held by a very small percentage of the total respondents.

items.title: Language Educator as an Experience Designer in XR-AI Environments
items.abstract: This chapter examines the convergence of extended reality and artificial intelligence in language education, focusing on immersive conversational agents. While XR-AI technologies offer notable affective and linguistic benefits for learners, the evolving responsibilities of teachers are frequently overlooked. To address this gap, this chapter investigates shifting educator roles through three conceptual pillars: a sociomaterial perspective, human-centered design thinking, and the human-in-the-loop principle. By synthesizing these core pillars with current research, the author proposes the Entangled Design Loop (EDL) framework. This pedagogical model outlines the actions teachers must take before, within, and beyond immersive environments. Ultimately, this framework equips language educators with actionable strategies for integrating smart technologies while ensuring that pedagogical decision-making remains decisively human.

items.title: Large language models for multimodal clinical predictive modeling: a systematic review
items.abstract: The electronic health record (EHR) comprises structured and unstructured data, both of which are integral for comprehensively representing patient history. The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has enabled the incorporation of unstructured data modalities into machine learning models that leverage EHR data. In this systematic review, we characterize studies that utilize LLM-enabled multimodal predictive modeling with EHR data. Following a screening of 641 studies, 57 met inclusion criteria. We identified three strategies for LLM-based multimodal integration: embedding, extraction, and text fusion. Delineated by the format of the unstructured data at the time of fusion, all strategies yielded performance gains (average 6.4% increase) over single modality models. LLMs facilitated modeling by generating note-embeddings for downstream prediction, extracting clinically informative variables, and summarizing long text documents prior to integration. Building on our review, we identified LLM-enhanced predictive modeling considerations that include sample size, interpretability, and computational costs. This study supports the potential value of LLMs for EHR-based predictive modeling and provides a framework for future multimodal modeling tools.

items.title: Learning about learning: A path from spin glasses to artificial intelligence
items.abstract: The Hopfield model, originally inspired by spin glasses, occupies a central place at the intersection of statistical mechanics, neural networks, and artificial intelligence. Despite its conceptual simplicity and broad applicability, it is rarely integrated into the undergraduate physics curriculum. We present the Hopfield model as a pedagogically rich framework that naturally unifies core topics from the undergraduate physics curriculum and that provides a concise introduction based on concepts such as a model's energy function, dynamics, and pattern stability. We discuss practical aspects of its simulation and provide simulation codes. We also propose problems designed to mirror research practice, which can be included in undergraduate classes.

items.title: Learning global and local representations for generalized category discovery in neurodegenerative diseases
items.abstract: Abstract Background Artificial intelligence (AI) has achieved notable success in closed‐set classification of neurodegenerative diseases, but its performance degrades significantly in more realistic open‐set settings, such as discovering rare or novel disease subtypes from unlabeled data that are not seen during training. Purpose This study introduces, to our knowledge, the first framework for generalized category discovery (GCD) in neurodegenerative diseases using MRI. It aims to leverage labeled data from known categories to automatically identify novel categories within unlabeled datasets. Methods We propose a GCD framework integrating semi‐supervised contrastive learning with global‐local representation learning to jointly optimize feature learning. Globally, we enforce consistency between weakly augmented views of the same instance by aligning their similarity relationships with other embeddings in a support queue. Locally, we treat neighborhood embeddings from the support queue as positive pairs for cross‐instance contrastive learning, enhancing fine‐grained discrimination. This dual strategy results in a unified learning objective that is applicable to both labeled and unlabeled data, effectively narrowing the representation gap among semantically similar instances. Results We evaluate our method on a benchmark dataset comprising six neurodegenerative diseases, with over 1500 patient samples. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework consistently outperforms representative state‐of‐the‐art methods. Specifically, our method achieves 66.02% Accuracy and 60.59% Normalized Mutual Information on all categories, and 54.53% Accuracy and 16.67% Normalized Mutual Information on novel categories, surpassing existing state‐of‐the‐art methods. Conclusions Our framework underscores the model's robustness and its practical value in discovering new neurodegenerative disease conditions, highlighting its potential for advancing open‐set diagnostic AI.

items.title: Legal Challenges of Artificial Intelligence in Global Health Policy
items.abstract: This article focuses on the legal challenges arising from the use of artificial intelligence in healthcare from the perspective of global health policy. While the active application of AI at various stages of healthcare demonstrates increasing efficiency, it also increases legal risks and highlights the necessity of an adapted legal framework. The article argues that the integration of artificial intelligence in healthcare is more challenging from a legal perspective than from a technological or ethical point of view, as it actively raises issues such as patient rights, the principle of informed consent, liability, and other related concerns, requiring coherent regulatory standards and coordinated policy responses. The authors propose a human-centered governance model that ensures the best possible balance, protects human rights and minimizes legal challenges arising from AI-related outcomes.

items.title: Legislative revisions to attendance mandates in german higher education and the experiences of academics: a case study informed by self-determination theory
items.abstract: This study investigates the impact of a legal regulation that relaxes mandatory attendance requirements in university courses in certain German states on academic practices. This study employed a descriptive design within a qualitative framework. The study group comprised six academics affiliated with Johannes Gutenberg University in Germany during the 2023–2024 academic year. Data were collected through semi-structured online interviews and analyzed using descriptive methods. The findings reveal that the legal regulation operates within a multi-layered structure. First, it was determined that higher education policies vary among the states in accordance with Germany’s federal structure, and that participation policies are shaped within this decentralized governance framework. Second, the emergence of the regulation was influenced by the positioning of students as autonomous and adult individuals, as well as by political and institutional pressure dynamics. Third, regulation enhances student autonomy and self-regulation skills, supports intrinsic motivation, and fosters innovation and academic competition in teaching processes. However, it was also determined that the regulation has led to significant negative consequences, such as a decline in faculty motivation, weakened classroom interaction, reduced course quality, and a diminished sense of responsibility among students. In conclusion, this study demonstrates that attendance policies in higher education encompass both pedagogical opportunities and structural risks, highlighting the necessity of balanced policies that strike a balance between student autonomy and the quality of teaching processes.

items.title: Leveraging Ethical Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Policy and Research Education
items.abstract: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) to education and policy-making offers them both hotly awaited possibilities and urgent ethical concerns. This conceptual paper, aims to understand how ethical AI models can drive data-informed decision-making that is in line with sustainability missions, ethical research practices and procedures. Though AI holds untapped tools for analyzing complex data, introducing prognosatory potential, and assisting policy creation, the paper negates that unchecked use might actually perpetuate biases, and foster irresponsibility and loss of transparency which will weakenedsocieties..A conceptual framework is developed in the paper that situates ethical AI as a connecting point between raw data and actionable decisions in the subject area of policy and research education. Using cutting-edge paradigms from data sciences, sustainability studies and educational literature: The pillars of the framework are four: (1) fairness and accountability of algorithmic models; (2) inclusion in data representations with stakeholders; (3) transparency in decision-making; and (4) outcomes towards sustainability for long-term social and ecological welfare..By incorporating these pillars into both policy and research education, the research identifies how institutions could guide their future African leaders and researchers to provide them with the competences to think critically with AI while ensuring ethical protection. The paper is further used to show how the adoption of ethical AI improves the legitimacy of evidence-based policymaking and is used to support changes in educational practices aimed on instilling responsibility through innovation. Informatics Research: This study adds to the ongoing discussion on the governance of AI, by presenting design frameworks based on education and policy that embedding ethics in the design of data-driven system itself. Ultimately, the study calls for human-centered approach to AI, which not only helps make decisions faster but also ensures that the technological advancements are on the path for sustainable and socially responsible futures.

items.title: Limitations of Computational Morality: Can We Morally Enhance Ourselves via AI?
items.abstract: Abstract Computational or machine ethics examines how morality could be implemented in machines and represented computationally. In the cognitive sciences, different architectures (rule-based and connectionist) have been proposed. Nevertheless, such approaches have limitations when incorporating ethical claims. With the rise of artificial intelligence, new ways of simulating moral expertise seem possible, where chatbots can serve as dialogue partners for moral orientation. However, as I will argue, such systems lack a theoretical grounding in metaethics, as do the former approaches. In order to align such systems ethically and ground them conceptually, a topography of moral competence must be developed. By outlining this topography, I will show some directions for further research and how such systems might enhance us morally.

items.title: Limitations of Generative AI in Content Creation: A Review
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools are now widely used to produce and support digital content such as stories, news items and social-media posts. Such tools can make a single piece of output look better, yet they also bring worries about originality, sameness across many outputs, bias, factual accuracy, creative control and ownership rights. This paper reviews five chosen scholarly works that look at creator responsibility, AI-supported story writing, prompting as a creative method, copyright, and bias in machine-written news. Read together, the studies indicate that a gain for one writer does not automatically become a gain for everyone: stories written with AI help may score higher while growing more alike. The remaining works point to the need for human fact-checking, the risk of skewed representation, the difficulty of turning unspoken creative know-how into written prompts, and unsettled questions about ownership and openness. We compare how the studies were carried out and what each contributes, draw out the shared challenges, and suggest where future work could head. Because only five hand-picked papers were examined and no exhaustive database search was run, this work is a focused narrative review rather than a systematic one.

items.title: Listening at scale: AI-assisted causal mapping for inclusive evaluation
items.abstract: Evaluation practice often faces a trade-off between depth and metrics, frequently resulting in the marginalisation of local voices. Traditional methods of coding texts, such as interviews, risk filtering diverse narratives through pre-defined, donor-driven frameworks, perpetuating a form of epistemic violence that prioritises ‘data’ over ‘story’. We propose an alternative: AI-assisted causal mapping as a method for ‘listening at scale’ using a zero-codebook approach where Generative AI serves as a ‘low-level’ assistant to extract causal links from large volumes of unstructured text without an imposed codebook. A case study of Tree Aid in Burkina Faso demonstrates how this method reveals complex outcomes which might be missed by models that use a pre-determined codebook. We introduce ‘soft recoding’ as a technique to align local narratives with donors’ conceptual frameworks without erasing original data. We conclude by reflecting on the tensions between bottom-up storytelling and top-down accountability, arguing that while AI has its own biases, rigorous human oversight can use it to amplify rather than silence marginalised voices.

items.title: LLM-enhanced Graph Contrastive Learning for Technology Flow Forecasting
items.abstract: Technology flow (TF) forecasting aims to predict whether a technology will be utilized by another, which is significant for future cross-integration technology innovation. Although existing methods have made substantial progress in intra-domain TF forecasting, inter-domain TF forecasting remains underexplored and faces several fundamental challenges. Specifically, semantic gaps between technologies from different domains hinder effective representation learning; historical inter-domain TFs are highly sparse, limiting the ability to learn reliable structural dependencies; and intra-domain and inter-domain TFs exhibit distinct flow patterns, which are difficult to model within a unified framework. To address these challenges, in this paper, we propose an LLM-enhanced Graph Contrastive Learning ( LGCL ) framework that supports both intra-domain and inter-domain TF forecasting. Specifically, we first leverage LLMs with bias-aware representation adjustment to generate semantically enriched and accurate technology representations to bridge gaps across multiple domains. Then, to mitigate the sparsity of inter-domain TF data, a technology co-occurrence view is incorporated to complement historical TF information. We further develop a non-negative contrastive learning module to integrate the TF and co-occurrence views, enabling effective representation alignment without relying on negative samples. In addition, we design decoupled loss functions to separately supervise intra-domain and inter-domain flows, mitigating the difficulty of jointly modeling their different flow patterns under a unified objective. Finally, experiments on real-world datasets validate the effectiveness of our approach and provide valuable insights into future technology flow trends. Our code is available at https://github.com/huijieliu2023/LGCL .

items.title: LLM-powered construction of antibiotic resistance datasets and knowledge graphs for accelerated antibiotic resistance gene discovery
items.abstract: Antibiotic resistance is a mounting global public health and development threat, with the misuse and overuse of antibiotics driving the rapid dissemination of multidrug-resistant pathogens. Developing next-generation small-molecule antibiotics requires in-depth investigation of resistance mechanisms and the identification of novel targets to overcome the limitations of current treatments. However, current strategies mainly rely on sequence-based homology search or models trained on manually curated datasets, which often suffer from outdated annotations, limited coverage, and high false-positive rates. These limitations hinder the identification of novel resistance targets. To address these limitations, we developed a Large Language Model (LLM)-powered automated pipeline that systematically mines resistance-related knowledge from full-text publications and supplementary materials, thereby supporting scalable and iterative data integration. Building on this framework, we constructed AResDB , a curated resource that integrates data from over 8570 published papers covering bacterial species, compounds, genes, mutations, phenotypes, and quantitative measurements. On this foundation, we constructed AResKG , a large-scale, multi-species knowledge graph of antibiotic resistance integrating 14 entity types, 27 relation types, and over 52.1 million triples. Experimental results based on AResKG demonstrate its effectiveness in improving the performance of commonly used machine learning methods for predicting gene-antibiotic resistance, compared with existing knowledge graphs. This work establishes a scalable, LLM-powered framework for antibiotic resistance research that advances the understanding of resistance mechanisms and accelerates the discovery of next-generation therapeutics.

items.title: Machine Learning and Intelligent Optimization Approaches for Robotic Manipulator Kinematic Modeling and Motion Planning: A Comprehensive Systematic Review
items.abstract: Kinematic modeling and path planning are critical problems in intelligent automation that directly affect the precision, adaptability, and safety of robotic arms. The ever-growing complexity of manipulators, including redundant DOFs, unique kinematic architectures, and environmental dynamics, has highlighted the drawbacks of classic analytical and Jacobian approaches in handling singularities, computational costs, and generalizability. Despite many reviews addressing particular problems such as inverse kinematics or reinforcement learning, an extensive overview of methodological development is yet to be provided. The sources for the literature review were mainly obtained from Google Scholar, while the publishing details for the selected articles were then cross-checked using the individual publishers’ and journal sites. The sources are divided into the following nine categories: analytical and hybrid inverse kinematics, neural networks, optimization, deep reinforcement learning, sampling- and learning-based motion planning, diffusion models, trajectory optimization, obstacle avoidance, and imitation learning. From the review, it is evident that there is a shift from traditional approaches such as analysis and optimization to AI-based methods like neural networks, deep reinforcement learning, and diffusion-based systems, with 105 studies published between 2022 and 2026. Some of the findings include MLP-based inverse kinematics (R2 > 0.99), meta-heuristic optimization resulting in a 4.75 × 10−4 cm position error, a 99.4% path-planning success rate through reinforcement learning, diffusion-based visuomotor control, and challenges facing intelligent robotic manipulation research.

items.title: Machine Learning-Based Forecasting of Energy Demand in Academic Buildings: Insights from a Case Study
items.abstract: This chapter presents the development of machine learning models for short-term energy demand forecasting in academic buildings, using a dataset from a higher education campus in Portugal. The dataset comprises quarter-hourly power demand data collected between January 2016 and February 2020, along with relevant exogenous variables. The study focuses on the impact of hyperparameter tuning on model performance, applying various algorithms—including Random Forest, Multivariate Adaptive Regression Splines, Artificial Neural Network, and Support Vector Machines. Grid Search and Random Search techniques were employed to optimize each model’s hyperparameters. Performance was evaluated using benchmarking metrics and visualization tools such as daily load profiles and scatter plots. The results indicate that the Random Forest and Artificial Neural Network models outperformed the others, particularly during school days and examination periods, which represent the most active times on campus. Beyond its technical contributions, this chapter illustrates how machine learning-based forecasting can support energy-aware decision-making in academic buildings, contributing to more efficient and sustainable campus operations. Moreover, the case study presented here highlights the pedagogical potential of integrating AI tools into sustainability curricula, fostering interdisciplinary learning and providing students and researchers with practical insights into the application of artificial intelligence in real-world energy systems.

items.title: Machine Unlearning: Methods, Evaluation, Challenges, and Future Directions
items.abstract: Trained machine learning models can hold on to traces of the data they were built from, including personal, outdated, incorrect, or unauthorized records. Deleting an entry from a database does not erase what a model has already absorbed from it. Machine unlearning tackles this gap by lowering or removing the effect of chosen training data, ideally without retraining the whole model every time. This review looks at five studies published between 2021 and 2025: one on coded machine unlearning, one on neuron masking, one on zero-shot unlearning, and two wider surveys of methods and evaluation. Together they trace a path from partition-based training designs and changes to model structure toward techniques that still work after the original training samples are gone, accompanied by increasingly systematic taxonomies and metrics. We compare the studies on the data access they assume, the unlearning strategy they use, their efficiency, how well they preserve utility, and how forgetting is verified. We also discuss the main open problems: the absence of a universal evaluation standard, the tension between forgetting and keeping performance on retained tasks, the risk of leftover information, and the difficulty of carrying these methods over to large language models and live systems. The work is a focused narrative review of the chosen papers; no new experiments or benchmark results are claimed. Our conclusion is that machine unlearning is a promising tool for privacy and model governance, but dependable use in practice requires measurable forgetting, clearly stated assumptions, and independent verification.

items.title: Managing generative-AI health information resilience: human resource capabilities and multilevel public health governance
items.abstract: The use of Conversational Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is growing as a way to interact with health information, especially for the public. This theory-based conceptual synthesis suggests a multilevel governance approach to reducing the likelihood for generated information to become unsafe action – GenAI health information resilience (GenAI-HIR). Its contribution is immediately usable and practical — deploying organizations and public-health actors and public-health actors can use the consequence-based control tiers, actor-specific safeguards, and domain-level audit anchors, and the proposed competency configuration still needs to be validated and is a research agenda for the future. Five conceptually distinct functions at the individual and workforce levels describe at which point protection may contribute to the decision pathway, but are not necessarily assumed to be empirically separable: recognize, interrogate, verify, contextualize, and escalate. Organizational capacity is limited to controls particular to created health information such as authorized sources, attainable human routing, incident monitoring and corrective action. Platform and regulatory conditions are constraints, safety, access, calibrated trust, and equity, outcomes. The framework was created using an expert guided purposive synthesis of the 62 sources that were retained, not a systematic review process. It distinguishes between an explanatory risk model and a normative control architecture and categorizes outputs with respect to type of output, severity, urgency, reversibility, context dependence, mitigation feasibility, and remaining risk. Falsification criteria are now included in six propositions. The candidate self-report indicators are kept as material for the cognitive interviewing only and must be correlated with behavioral vignettes before use for psychometric purposes. GenAI-HIR is therefore not a validated scale, certification standard or replacement for accessible professional care; it is a model for competency that can be falsified in future research and a governance structure that can be audited for current implementation.

items.title: Mapping Human Rights Scholarship in India: A Bibliometric and Thematic Review of Scopus-Indexed Research, 2016-2026
items.abstract: Human rights have become a pervasive vocabulary in Indian legal and social science research, yet the structure and direction of this expanding literature have rarely been examined systematically. This review maps 457 Scopus-indexed journal articles on human rights with at least one Indian institutional affiliation, published between 2016 and 2026, using performance analysis and science-mapping techniques. Annual output grew more than five-fold, from 14 articles in 2016 to 75 in 2025 and 82 in 2026, a compound annual growth rate of about 20.5 per cent. The literature is highly dispersed: the 457 articles appeared in 318 journals, 36 of which account for one-third of the output, and 93 per cent of the 1,516 authors contributed only one article. Citation impact is modest (median one citation; 36.3 per cent uncited; dataset h-index 22). Keyword co-occurrence analysis identifies six principal clusters: constitutional equality and discrimination; public health, pandemic and surveillance; artificial intelligence and intellectual property; climate change, displacement and the rights of nature; data protection and international law; and sustainable development and consumer protection. Thematic evolution shows a shift from trade-related intellectual property and health policy in 2016-2020 to COVID-19 and constitutional dignity in 2021-2023, and to artificial intelligence, data protection and climate change in 2024-2026. In contrast, the institutions through which rights are enforced receive very little attention: police, prisons and custody appear in about 2 per cent of articles, caste and Dalit concerns in 2.2 per cent, and the National Human Rights Commission in only three articles (0.7 per cent), none of which takes a commission as its object of study. The review argues that Indian human rights scholarship has undergone a “technological and regulatory turn” that risks neglecting the accountability of the coercive state, and proposes a research agenda centred on enforcement institutions, caste and gender intersections, and data-driven evaluation.
